subtopics.title: Selling on Credit — the Invoice and the Debtors Journal

questions.question: The source document that creates a debt when goods are sold on credit is:
options: The numbered invoice, issued in duplicate
A cash register slip
A credit note
A receipt

questions.question: The Debtors Journal records:
options: All sales, cash and credit
Credit sales of trading stock only
Money received from debtors
Goods returned by debtors

questions.question: A business accepts the risk and admin of credit selling because:
options: Cash is unsafe to handle
SARS requires credit sales
Customers buy more and sooner on credit — refusing it hands them to competitors
Credit sales carry higher prices by law

subtopics.title: Recording and Posting the Debtors Journal

questions.question: Invoice 61: goods R2 000 at 25% mark-up on cost. The DJ line reads:
options: Sales R2 000; Cost of Sales R1 600
Sales R2 000; Cost of Sales R1 500
Sales R1 600; Cost of Sales R2 000
Sales R2 000 only — cost is ignored for credit sales

questions.question: The DJ's month-end totals (Sales R4 500, CoS R3 600) post to the general ledger as:
options: Debit Sales; credit Debtors Control; debit Trading Stock; credit Cost of Sales
Debit Debtors Control R4 500; credit Sales R4 500; debit Cost of Sales R3 600; credit Trading Stock R3 600
Debit Bank R4 500; credit Sales R4 500
Debit Debtors Control R8 100; credit Trading Stock R8 100

questions.question: The timing architecture of debtors posting is:
options: Everything posts monthly
Everything posts daily
Personal accounts daily; control and other general ledger accounts monthly by totals
Personal accounts yearly; control daily

questions.question: Why is Sales credited even though no money has been received?
options: It is an error tolerated for simplicity
Sales is only credited when cash arrives
The debtor pays interest in the meantime
The sale was earned when made — the Sales account does not care when the money arrives

questions.question: The credit note is best described as:
options: The invoice's mirror — a numbered document reducing the customer's debt
Proof of payment
A second invoice
A bank document

questions.question: Dube returns undamaged goods (R500, cost R400). The DAJ line shows:
options: Debtors Allowances R500 only
Debtors Allowances R500 AND Cost of Sales R400 — the goods return to stock
Cost of Sales R400 only
Debtors Allowances R400 and Cost of Sales R500

questions.question: Naidoo keeps the scratched kettle for R150 off. The cost column:
options: Carries the kettle's cost
Carries R150
Stays empty — no goods moved, so no stock entry exists
Carries half the kettle's cost

questions.question: Debtors Allowances is kept separate from Sales because:
options: Sales may never be reduced
The two accounts belong to different ledgers
Allowances are not part of turnover
Management needs gross sales AND the coming-back amount as separate signals — rising allowances flag quality problems

subtopics.title: The Debtors Ledger at Month End

questions.question: L. Dube: debits R2 000 and R1 000, credit R500. Her balance is:
options: R2 500 debit — she owes the business R2 500
R3 500 debit
R2 500 credit
R1 500 debit

questions.question: The list of debtors totals R3 850. Debtors Control shows debits R4 500 and credits R650. The comparison:
options: Fails by R650
Agrees at R3 850 — as it must, since both are built from the same journals
Cannot be made until year end
Fails by R4 500

questions.question: Which set of measures keeps credit selling safe?
options: Higher prices for credit customers
Refusing all returns
Credit limits, monthly statements, chasing overdue debts promptly, and separating recording from receiving
Keeping debtor balances secret

questions.question: The page-per-person book under the counter corresponds to:
options: The Debtors Ledger — one personal account per customer
The general ledger
The Debtors Journal
The trial balance

questions.question: 'The whole street on one line' is:
options: The Sales account
The invoice book
Mrs Dube's page
Debtors Control — the general ledger's summary of all debtors

questions.question: The 'lock' between the pages and the street-line is:
options: The sum of all personal pages must equal the control account's balance
Both must equal the Sales total
The pages must always show more than the line
A physical lock on the ledger drawer

subtopics.title: The Week Mrs Dube Changed Her Mind

questions.question: The returned R500 shirt (cost R400) triggers:
options: Only a credit to her page
Her page credited R500 AND the shelf regaining R400, which stops being cost of sales
Only a stock entry
A new invoice

questions.question: The rule 'follow the goods' means:
options: Deliveries must be tracked by vehicle
The debtor's page is only updated when goods move
The cost column writes only when goods physically move — back to the shelf or not at all
Sales follow the customer

questions.question: Sales R4 500 with R650 returned versus sales R3 850 with nothing returned:
options: Identical shops — only the net matters
The first shop is healthier
The second shop must have a control problem
Same net, different stories — separate books keep the difference visible

questions.question: A credit limit is described as 'the reason the shop can keep saying yes' because:
options: It caps each name's risk, keeping total exposure survivable
It increases every month automatically
It replaces the need for statements
It guarantees payment

questions.question: Monthly statements do two quiet jobs:
options: Advertise and decorate
Remind politely and surface disputes early
Replace invoices and credit notes
Calculate interest and tax

questions.question: Why should the person writing the debtor pages not receive the payments?
options: Writing and counting need different skills
It slows the queue
Division of duties — two sets of hands, with a paper trail between them
Customers prefer paying the owner
